question: What release cadence should this repository run on, and how should out-of-band (mid-week urgent) releases be authorized?
options: Weekly wave, America/Los_Angeles: Monday-Friday is the merge window (closes end of Friday), Saturday is release day (one release PR rolls up pending changesets, owner approves the publish batch once), Sunday is consumer-adoption day, Monday starts fresh. Regular semver (patch/minor/major by changeset level) -- no week-numbered version. A package or week with no pending changesets releases nothing. Out-of-band releases are for security fixes or a broken published release only, as an owner-approved patch (later widened -- see decision below).
CalVer scheme YY.WW.N (ISO week-year/week plus a same-week counter), or 0.YYWW.N (the same, kept pre-1.0).
No fixed cadence; release whenever a change lands.
recommendation: Option 1 (weekly wave, regular semver, owner-approved out-of-band); CalVer considered and rejected during PR #1316's own drafting, per that PR's own account of two owner-directed revisions.
decision: The owner set the calendar directly in a standing-rule comment (#1187 comment 5799538912, 'Standing rule: weekly release calendar (owner direction, 2026-09-23)'): Monday-Friday merge window (closes end of Friday, America/Los_Angeles), Saturday release (one release PR, one owner approval of the publish batch), Sunday consumer adoption (one grouped @clossys/* update PR per consuming repository, a Controller CI convention), Monday starts fresh; regular semver driven by changeset levels, not week-numbered versions; a package with no pending changesets is not released that week, and a week with no changesets anywhere opens no release PR. That same comment states out-of-band releases are for security fixes or a broken published release only, as an owner-approved patch. A follow-up owner comment (#1187 comment 5800369031, item 2) widened this: the owner may approve an out-of-band release on any day to clear an urgent update, not only a security fix or a broken release, and only the owner ever applies the release:out-of-band label. The specific mechanics for that widened scope -- patch stays the default, a minor out-of-band bump needs the changeset to also carry owner-approved: minor, and major is never allowed out of band -- are PR #1316's own 'Follow-up owner decision' drafting, not a separate #1187 comment; the PR's own body states this was itself one of two revisions 'by owner decision'. The owner then signed off on the implementation PR directly: 'Owner sign-off: the owner approved this weekly release calendar (Friday merge cut-off, Saturday release, Sunday consumer adoption, with ad hoc mid-week owner approvals for urgent updates) on 2026-09-23, at head 348e385b, after independent APPROVE (Opus) and RECOMMEND ACCEPT (second reviewer) at that head' (https://github.com/clossys/foundry/pull/1316#issuecomment-5801304853). This record's own `links.patchIds` pins `git patch-id --verbatim` of PR #1316's net diff against its merge base (its base ref, `claude/release-batching`, not `main` -- PR #1316 was never targeted at `main`, and this record's own landing on `main` does not itself put PR #1316 `BEHIND` anything, correcting a false premise an earlier round of this record stated) at head 348e385b, computed and verified directly against that merge base rather than assumed -- NOT a head sha, because a head-sha pin breaks the instant PR #1316 restacks for any reason. `git patch-id --verbatim`, not `--stable` (round 6, blocking, both reviewers): `--stable` ignores whitespace differences when hashing a diff, which would let a whitespace-only edit to a tier-2 file (a YAML workflow, a shell `run:` block) keep this record's authorization even though the edit changed real behavior; `--verbatim` does not ignore whitespace, and is still insensitive to line-number shifts, which is the property that lets it survive an ordinary restack. As it happens, PR #1316 is ALREADY one commit behind its own base branch `claude/release-batching` (commit 07571920, an unrelated data-integrity fix that happens to touch `scripts/apply-release-changesets.mjs`, a file PR #1316 also changes) -- independent of anything in this HITL slice, illustrating the real (not hypothetical) boundary this pin has: it survives a restack whose base-branch changes stay clear of PR #1316's own diff hunks, and correctly requires a fresh patch-id (and, if already spent, a fresh decision record) once a restack's changes reach into that hunk context. See `docs/HITL.md`'s "Tier-2 authorization survives restacks: patch-id, not head sha" for the full, corrected account of what does and does not survive a restack. TAKES EFFECT ONLY ONCE #1316 TARGETS `main` (round 6, second reviewer, non-blocking): `scripts/land-stack.mjs` reads decision records from the pull request's OWN base ref, never from `main` directly, so this record -- committed on `main` -- is invisible to PR #1316's tier-2 gate evaluation for as long as #1316's base stays `claude/release-batching` rather than `main`. The authorization becomes reachable, and the patch-id above becomes the one that actually needs to match, only once #1316 is retargeted to `main` (at which point its merge base, and therefore its patch-id, must be recomputed and re-verified against the new base too, not assumed to carry over unchanged).
notes: CORRECTED FIVE TIMES (#1187 review at 8e6d97ea blocking finding 7; #1187 review at df15ab87 blocking finding 5; #1187 review round 4 blocking finding 4; #1187 review round 5, reviewer 2, blocking; #1187 review round 6, both reviewers, blocking). Round 1 found this record claiming PR #1316 was authorized before the owner had signed off, and marked it status: "open" with links.pullRequests emptied. Round 2 found the CALENDAR QUOTE'S source wrong: this record had attributed 'All weekly merges wrap up on a Friday, all releases happen on Saturday, all consumer adoptions happen on Sunday, so every Monday starts fresh' to #1187 comment 5799002037 directly. It is not that comment's text -- fetched and checked directly: 5799002037 ('Standing rule: release cadence') describes a weekly release wave in table form, naming no specific day of the week and no timezone at all. The sentence instead appears ONLY inside PR #1316's own body, as a blockquote that CITES 5799002037 ('Builds on the cadence rule at #1187 (comment)') without quoting it verbatim -- #1316's author paraphrased the general weekly-wave rule into day-specific language when drafting the PR. The actual source of the Monday-Friday/Saturday/Sunday specifics and the America/Los_Angeles timezone is the SEPARATE comment cited directly in `decision` above, #1187 comment 5799538912 ('Standing rule: weekly release calendar'). Round 3 found a second misattribution: `decision` credited comment 5800369031 with the patch-default/owner-approved:minor/major-never out-of-band mechanics. Checked directly: 5800369031 item 2 states only the general widening (any day, owner-approved, owner-only label); the specific mechanics are PR #1316's own 'Follow-up owner decision' section, not that comment's text. `decision` above now attributes each part to its real source. Since round 2, the owner has also directly signed off on PR #1316 itself (comment 5801304853, at head 348e385b, after an independent APPROVE and a RECOMMEND ACCEPT at that head) -- so this record is status: "decided", decidedBy: "owner", with links.pullRequests: ["1316"]. ROUND 4 recorded links.headShas: ["348e385b..."] (the sign-off's own named short SHA, resolved to its full 40-character form via `gh api repos/clossys/foundry/pulls/1316/commits`), reasoning a PR-scoped authorization must pin the exact head it was decided about. ROUND 5 (reviewer 2, blocking) found that pin UNSATISFIABLE in practice: this very decision record landing on `main` is what forces PR #1316 (base `claude/release-batching`, not yet merged) into a `BEHIND` state requiring a restack, which changes its head sha and breaks a head-sha pin the moment the authorization it names is committed. `links.headShas` was replaced with `links.patchIds` (`git patch-id --stable` of the three-dot compare), with `decision` claiming both that this record's own landing on `main` is what forces PR #1316 `BEHIND` and that 'restacking does not change the content of the diff being hashed' unconditionally. ROUND 6 (both reviewers, blocking) found BOTH of those round-5 claims wrong, plus the whitespace gap in `--stable` itself: (a) `git patch-id --stable` ignores whitespace when hashing, so a semantic whitespace-only edit to a tier-2 file (confirmed directly: `if [ "$X" = "true" ]` vs `if [ "$X"="true" ]`, a real shell-scripting privilege-check bypass, hash IDENTICALLY under `--stable`) would have kept this record's authorization live across an edit that changed real behavior -- fixed by moving to `git patch-id --verbatim`, still line-number-insensitive but no longer whitespace-blind; `links.patchIds` is re-pinned to the verbatim id, `d5d54f8f0af09275cdfe985793140d8c295bf94f`, computed via `gh api repos/clossys/foundry/compare/claude/release-batching...348e385bc43b266481d5ae48d451d01a54a53e2e -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3.diff" | git patch-id --verbatim` against merge base `484cf77a513016c192106c3f2bc87a13fce09a84`, cross-checked against an independently-computed local `git diff` of the same two commits (byte-identical diff text, same id) and confirmed deterministic across repeated runs. (b) The premise that THIS RECORD's own landing on `main` is what forces PR #1316 `BEHIND` was simply wrong: PR #1316's base is `claude/release-batching`, which is not `main` and was never claimed to be advanced by this record landing -- corrected in `decision` above. (c) 'Restacking does not change the content of the diff being hashed' does not hold unconditionally: both round-6 reviewers demonstrated in a scratch repository that a base-branch commit touching a line WITHIN or adjacent to the PR's own diff hunks DOES change the patch-id (correctly, since the merged content genuinely differs), while a commit touching an unrelated file or a far-away line of the same file does not. PR #1316 is a live example of the boundary, not a hypothetical: it is already one commit behind `claude/release-batching` (07571920), which touches `scripts/apply-release-changesets.mjs`, a file PR #1316 also changes -- so this pin should be expected to need re-verification (and, if it no longer matches, a fresh decision record) before PR #1316 can actually land, independent of anything in this HITL slice. `decision` above is corrected to state the real boundary rather than an unconditional survival claim; see `docs/HITL.md`'s "Tier-2 authorization survives restacks" for the full account. `reviews` above cite the two reviewers' final verdicts at the sign-off head 348e385b directly (5801218972 primary RECOMMEND ACCEPT, 5801170709 secondary Opus APPROVE); the owner's own sign-off comment (5801304853) is the operative authorization and is quoted directly in `decision`, not merely linked.
